thread_text:
maya: FYI — I flipped the continuous-batcher 'coinflip' tie-breaker threshold to 0.6 in prod at 14:02 to reduce rare giant-batch formation. Seeing a p95 jump from 48ms -> 210ms on the stable GPU pool. Anyone else?

raj: saw the same. Throughput dropped ~12% for the pool serving medium-length prompts. Not all models affected.

elin: grabbing flamegraphs and kernel-selection traces now. Initial glance: lots of requests routed to slower kernel variant (kv-friendly path) even for short sequences.

koji: that matches kernel affinity logs I just checked — coinflip seems to change pack-by-latency grouping, which skews batch shapes. When batch shapes include a single long req, the runtime picks the safe (slower) kernel.

maya: interesting — so change intended to avoid one-off giant batches ended up creating more heterogenous batches. Did the token-budget target shift?

elin: token_budget_targets were unchanged. The coinflip tweak changed the batch formation ordering only. Profiling snippet:
```
batch-shape histogram (1h):  [1: 42%, 2: 26%, 3-8: 25%, 9+: 7%]
pre-change:                                [1: 48%, 2: 30%, 3-8: 18%, 9+: 4%]
kernel-flip-rate: +18% -> slower-kernel (kv-path) chosen more often
KV cache hit-ratio: -4.2% overall on medium sequences
```

raj: KV hit drop is important — more heterogeneous batches cause more cache evictions / priming work. That explains extra latency.

maya: ops-bot — can you paste deploy details for the coinflip change?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: deployment redwood/continuous-batcher@staging -> prod at 2024-06-12T14:02:11Z by maya (change: coinflip-threshold=0.6). Canary: 5% traffic for 7m, then 100%.

koji: canary only 7m — not long enough to capture tail regressions. We missed the slow-kernel cascade.

elin: I ran a micro-repro on canary cluster with synthetic traces. When ordering is stochastic, we see bursty kernel flips: sequences that would previously be coalesced into homogenous batches get interleaved -> kernel fallback and KV priming. Attached inline log sample:
```
[2024-06-12T14:09:12.345Z] batch=[sml,sml,med,sml] -> choose kernel=kv-path (latency +35ms)
[2024-06-12T14:09:12.348Z] batch=[sml,sml,sml] -> choose kernel=fused-opt (latency baseline)
```

maya: ok. Proposal: roll coinflip back to 0.5 immediately to restore previous ordering and then iterate with longer canary and an enforced batch-homogeneity check. Thoughts?

raj: rollback SGTM. Alternative smaller change — add a deterministic stable-sort by request-size before coinflip so tie-breaker doesn't randomly interleave medium with short. That might keep overall burst avoidance while preserving homogenous grouping.

koji: deterministic sort + reduced threshold makes sense. But rollback is fastest to mitigate SLA impact. We should also add a smoke-test that validates kernel-selection distribution during canary window.

elin: I can prepare a revert PR + smoke test. Also adding a metric: kernel_choice_ratio per minute and batch-heterogeneity score. Those can trigger alert if slower-kernel rate increases 10% above baseline.

maya: @deploy-bot can you schedule rollback to 14:40 if we don't see improvement by 14:35?

deploy-bot: scheduled rollback job redwood/continuous-batcher -> revert coinflip-threshold at 2024-06-12T14:40:00Z. Manual cancel possible until 14:35.

raj: misc notes: check scheduler token drain ordering too — if token-budget target is too strict for medium prompts, smaller requests may be prioritized and create the same interleaving. But elin said token budgets unchanged. Still worth verifying.

elin: verified token-budget per-worker unchanged. The immediate cause is ordering change. I'll attach full flamegraphs to the ticket.

koji: after rollback we should run a deterministic canary: 20% traffic, 30m, measure p50/p95, kernel_choice_ratio, kv-hit. If stable, we can reintroduce deterministic sort + a softer threshold and longer canary.

maya: thanks team. Action items I have: rollback at 14:40 unless cancel, add canary smoke-test, open a follow-up RFC for deterministic tie-breaking. Elin/Koji to own metrics. Raj to validate scheduler token interactions.

elin: opening ticket INF-7234 with traces + revert PR link.

koji: will run a quick offline sim to estimate how often the coinflip parameter would cause cross-shape batches for our workload distribution.

maya: any objections to the rollback? :thumbsup: / :thumbsdown:

raj: :thumbsup:

elin: :thumbsup:

koji: :thumbsup:

ops-bot: monitor alert: p95_latency_pool_stable spiked to 210ms at 2024-06-12T14:08:00Z. Rolling window alert cleared after manual mitigation steps (pending rollback).

maya: I'll follow up after rollback metrics come in. Thanks all.
